name: spelunk
description: One search box for file names, code and Git history across every repo in the workspace.

webview/context.when: webviewId == 'spelunk' && webviewSection == 'result' && remoteHost != 'github' && remoteHost != 'gitlab' && remoteHost != 'bitbucket' && remoteHost != 'gitea' && remoteHost != 'azure'
webviewId == 'spelunk' && webviewSection == 'result' && remoteHost != 'github' && remoteHost != 'gitlab' && remoteHost != 'bitbucket' && remoteHost != 'gitea' && remoteHost != 'azure'

enumDescriptions: ⌘P / Ctrl+P opens Spelunk; Quick Open moves to ⌥⌘P / Ctrl+Alt+P.
⇧⌘F / Ctrl+Shift+F opens Spelunk; Quick Open is unchanged. VS Code's Search view then has no key: open it from the Activity Bar, or bind workbench.view.search yourself.
No default shortcut. Bind spelunk.open yourself.
Ignore case: retry also finds Retry and RETRY.
Match case: retry finds only retry.
Match case only when the query has a capital letter: retry finds Retry, but RetryPolicy doesn't find retrypolicy.
spelunk.search.caseSensitive.description: How capital letters match by default. A case: operator in the query always wins.

spelunk.search.wholeWord.description: Match whole words by default, so retry doesn't match retryCount. A word: operator in the query always wins.

enumDescriptions: A word matches its exact text only.
A word also finds file names that have its letters in order, as Quick Open does: rtrypol finds retry_policy.py.
spelunk.search.match.description: How a word matches file names by default. A match: in the query always wins. Lines of code always match exactly.

spelunk.search.useExcludeSettings.markdownDescription: Leave out the files `#files.exclude#` and `#search.exclude#` hide, as VS Code's own search does. A note under the results counts them, and its Show them adds `excludes:no` to the query. Off, every indexed file shows.

spelunk.search.seedFromSelection.description: Search the editor's selection when the search key is pressed in the editor. Off, the panel reopens with the last query, as it does with nothing selected.

spelunk.search.typingDelayMs.description: Milliseconds to wait after a keystroke before searching.

spelunk.search.timeLimitMs.description: How long one search may run, in milliseconds, before it shows what it found so far and says the results are truncated. Raise it for very large workspaces.

spelunk.caseSensitive.deprecationMessage: Moved to spelunk.search.caseSensitive. Spelunk moves a value saved here when it starts.
spelunk.caseSensitive.markdownDeprecationMessage: Moved to `#spelunk.search.caseSensitive#`. Spelunk moves a value saved here when it starts.

spelunk.wholeWord.deprecationMessage: Moved to spelunk.search.wholeWord. Spelunk moves a value saved here when it starts.
spelunk.wholeWord.markdownDeprecationMessage: Moved to `#spelunk.search.wholeWord#`. Spelunk moves a value saved here when it starts.

spelunk.typingDelayMs.deprecationMessage: Moved to spelunk.search.typingDelayMs. Spelunk moves a value saved here when it starts.
spelunk.typingDelayMs.markdownDeprecationMessage: Moved to `#spelunk.search.typingDelayMs#`. Spelunk moves a value saved here when it starts.

spelunk.results.count.description: Results per page when the query has no count: operator.

enumDescriptions: Best match first: definitions and file-name matches first; tests, vendored and generated files last.
Path order, A to Z: repo by repo, then by path, then by line.
Path order, Z to A: repo by repo, paths from Z to A; lines stay top to bottom.
Recently changed, newest first: by when each file last changed, its uncommitted edits or newest commit.
Recently changed, oldest first: the files changed longest ago first.
spelunk.results.order.description: How results from current files are sorted when the query has no order: operator. The order menu and arrow in each results heading set it too. Commits are always newest first.

spelunk.results.contextLines.description: Lines to show above and below each code match in the results, from 0 to 3. The Context buttons in the Code heading set it too.

spelunk.defaultCount.deprecationMessage: Moved to spelunk.results.count. Spelunk moves a value saved here when it starts.
spelunk.defaultCount.markdownDeprecationMessage: Moved to `#spelunk.results.count#`. Spelunk moves a value saved here when it starts.

spelunk.order.deprecationMessage: Moved to spelunk.results.order. Spelunk moves a value saved here when it starts.
spelunk.order.markdownDeprecationMessage: Moved to `#spelunk.results.order#`. Spelunk moves a value saved here when it starts.

spelunk.open.trigger.description: Whether a single click or a double click opens a result. A single click always previews.

spelunk.open.preview.description: Open results in a preview editor that the next result replaces.

spelunk.open.closeOnOpen.description: Hide the search panel after opening a result, except to the side. F4 keeps stepping through the results.

enumDescriptions: Last 6 months
Last 2 years
Everything
spelunk.index.historyDepth.description: How much Git history to index for author:, msg: and history search.

spelunk.index.symbols.description: Index symbol definitions for symbol: (s:) and kind: (k:).

spelunk.index.exclude.description: Glob patterns never indexed, in current files or in history. A pattern without a slash matches at any depth, a trailing slash names a folder (node_modules/), and a leading slash anchors it at the repo root (/build).

spelunk.index.maxFileSizeKB.description: Skip files larger than this. A Jupyter notebook counts only its cells' code and notes, not its outputs and plots.

spelunk.index.notebookOutputs.description: Also search the text a Jupyter notebook's code cells printed or returned. Off, only cells' code and notes are searched; plots and other images never are.

spelunk.index.mergedBranches.description: Also search the commits made on branches that were merged in, each under its own author and dated by when it was merged, and show a merge as only the lines it changed itself. Off, history follows the checked-out branch's own line, and a merge holds its whole branch. On a large repo with many merges, history takes longer to read and more memory.

spelunk.index.location.description: Where indexes are stored: an absolute path, or one starting with ~. Anything else stores them in the default place. Never synced, because paths differ between computers.

spelunk.index.vendoredFolders.description: Folder names, at any depth, that hold someone else's code or a build's. Their files match is:vendored and rank last.

spelunk.index.generatedSuffixes.description: File name endings that mark files a tool wrote. Those files, and files with @generated or a DO NOT EDIT … generated note near the top, match is:generated and rank low.

spelunk.index.codeownersFiles.description: Where to look for each repo's CODEOWNERS file, relative to its root, for owner:. The first one found is used.

spelunk.index.commitCheckSeconds.description: How often, in seconds, to check Git for new commits, so history search and watches see them.

spelunk.ui.showParsedQuery.description: Show the parsed query as chips under the search box.

spelunk.ui.recentQueries.description: How many recent queries to remember.

spelunk.ui.previewContextLines.description: Lines the file preview shows above and below the selected match.

spelunk.ui.syntaxHighlighting.description: Color code in results and the preview with the color theme's syntax colors, using the language grammars VS Code colors the editor with.

enumDescriptions: Follow `#editor.renderWhitespace#`.
Mark no whitespace.
Mark indentation, trailing whitespace and runs of spaces between words.
Mark the whitespace of the matched lines.
Mark trailing whitespace only.
Mark every space and tab.
spelunk.ui.renderWhitespace.markdownDescription: Which whitespace the preview marks, as faint dots for spaces and arrows for tabs. `editor` follows `#editor.renderWhitespace#`.

query.description: The query, as typed in the search box.

name.description: What the empty box calls it; the query itself when left out.

watch.description: Tell me when new commits match it (history queries only): the bell in the empty box.

spelunk.ui.pinnedQueries.description: Queries starred in the empty box, top first, each with an optional name. Set it in a workspace's settings to share the pins with everyone who opens the workspace; pinning then saves there.

spelunk.watch.notify.description: Pop up a notification when new commits by others match a watched pinned query. Off, the pin's count of new commits still shows in the empty box.

spelunk.permalinks.hosts.markdownDescription: Which kind of Git host a server is, for **Copy Permalink** on the right-click menu of a result, which asks the first time it meets a server it can't place and saves your answer here. Spelunk knows github.com, gitlab.com, bitbucket.org, codeberg.org and dev.azure.com, and guesses from a name with `github`, `gitlab`, `gitea` or `forgejo` in it; add any other server by the host name in its remote's URL, for example `{ "git.acme.corp": "gitlab" }`.

spelunk.agent.shareWindow.markdownDescription: Let the `spelunk` command in a terminal, and AI agents such as Claude Code and Copilot, search the folders open in this window, with live results. They only read; nothing they ask can change a file or an index. Off, they search the saved index instead, through a background reader. Reachable only by your user account on this computer.

spelunk.agent.offerToCopilot.markdownDescription: List Spelunk's read-only search tools for Copilot and other agents in VS Code (VS Code 1.101 or later). Off, VS Code's agents don't see Spelunk.

spelunk.agent.timeLimitMs.markdownDescription: How long one search from the `spelunk` command or an agent may run before it returns what it found, marked as stopped early. Longer than the panel's #spelunk.search.timeLimitMs#, since an agent can't tell an incomplete answer to try again.

spelunk.editor.workspaceSymbols.markdownDescription: List Spelunk's definitions in **Go to Symbol in Workspace** (⌘T, or `#` in Quick Open): the functions, classes and types in every indexed repo and language, found by typing a few of their letters in order. A definition a language server also lists shows once.

enumDescriptions: Go to Definition and Find References never use Spelunk.
Spelunk answers only when no language server does.
Spelunk's answers are added to the language servers' answers.
spelunk.editor.definitions.markdownDescription: Whether **Go to Definition** (F12) and **Find References** (⇧F12) use Spelunk's index. Spelunk goes by the name's spelling, not its meaning, so another definition with the same name can come up too; it keeps to the file's language when that language has any.

spelunk.editor.includeGeneratedAndVendor.markdownDescription: Include definitions and uses in generated and vendored files (see #spelunk.index.generatedSuffixes# and #spelunk.index.vendoredFolders#) in Go to Symbol in Workspace, Go to Definition and Find References, marked `generated` or `vendored` and listed last.

enumDescriptions: The Generate query button and a question ending in ? do nothing.
Anthropic's Claude turns the question into a Spelunk query (needs an API key: Spelunk: Set Anthropic API Key).
spelunk.ask.provider.markdownDescription: Who turns a question in plain words into a Spelunk query. Type a question ending in `?`, or press Ask: the query it becomes shows under the box and runs. Only the question goes to the provider, never your code.

spelunk.ask.model.markdownDescription: The provider's model that writes the query. `claude-opus-5-5` is the default; `claude-haiku-4-5` answers faster and costs less. **Spelunk: Choose Ask Model** lists the models your API key can use and sets this.

enumDescriptions: Answers fastest and costs least: enough for most questions.
Thinks a little longer about the question.
Reads the question carefully; slower and costs more.
Thinks as long as the model allows; slowest and costs the most.
spelunk.ask.effort.markdownDescription: How long the model thinks before writing the query. Raise it when a question keeps becoming the wrong query. A level the model doesn't take becomes the nearest it does (Claude 4.5 and older take none); **Spelunk: Choose Ask Model** shows each model's levels.

spelunk.ask.shareNames.markdownDescription: Send the repo names and the CODEOWNERS team names with the question, so a query can name them (`repo:web`, `owner:payments-core`). Off, the question goes alone.
